diagnostic_evidence.quote: and the choice of basis vectors does not matter due to invariance of wedge product under change of orthonomal basis

issues.failure_explanation: For an m-rectifiable set without a chosen orientation, tau^S(x) = e_1(x)∧…∧e_m(x) is only defined up to sign: replacing the orthonormal basis of the tangent space by an orientation-reversing one flips the wedge product, hence flips [S](omega). The claimed invariance 'under change of orthonormal basis' holds only for orientation-preserving changes, so the current [S] is determined only up to sign and is not unique as stated.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require S to be an oriented rectifiable set (or fix an orientation a priori) in the Definition; all later uses already work with chosen orientations, so no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The Definition block's assertion of a unique current associated to a rectifiable set fails; the subsequent background identities and the RKHS embedding of [S] inherit an ambiguous object.
issues.title: Current associated to a rectifiable set is not unique as defined
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local condition (a fixed orientation) preserves the definition's content and every downstream use; no new lemma or construction is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: so that $S_{a,b}^{+,\perp}$ is a half circle in the plane perpendicular to $a$

issues.failure_explanation: For a unit half-circle C = {u: u⊥e, u·β ≥ 0}, parametrizing u(θ)=cosθ β + sinθ γ over θ∈[−π/2,π/2] gives ∫_C u dH^1 = β·∫_{−π/2}^{π/2}cosθ dθ = 2β_T, not (π/2)β_T. The asserted value is a specific integral evaluation that is false; with the correct value 2β_T the derived cylindrical Dirac weights would be −2Σδ_{c_j}γ_j rather than −(π/2)Σδ_{c_j}, which would make the edge coefficient of the derived metric equal to 4 and contradict the quoted Theorem thm:added-1 (pi²/4). The claimed agreement with NC_disc_met therefore holds only through this false value.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-evaluate the half-circle integral (value 2β_T), recompute the cylindrical weights, and rederive the constants in \eqref{NC_delta} and \eqref{realembedding}; additionally reconcile the resulting edge coefficient with the quoted Theorem thm:added-1, since with the corrected integral the agreement claimed in the source no longer holds.
issues.overall_effect: The cylindrical Dirac weights (and hence the edge term of the Dirac delta form \eqref{NC_delta}, the real-valued embedding \eqref{realembedding}, and the claimed agreement of the resulting scalar product with the discrete normal-cycle metric of Theorem thm:added-1) are mis-normalized; the compression pipeline then targets a wrongly scaled functional.
issues.title: Half-circle unit-normal integral mis-evaluated (pi/2 instead of 2)
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained (recompute one standard integral and propagate constants, then reconcile the normalization with the quoted theorem), and the compression algorithm and its guarantees survive with a comparable result, but the exactness claim for the decomposition must be re-derived rather than locally patched.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: one may check the resulting scalar product of $N(\mathcal{T}),N(\mathcal{T}') \in W^{*}$ of \cref{NC_delta} agrees with \cref{NC_disc_met} derived in \cite{NCpaper}

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's own cylindrical section derives N(T)^cyl = −(π/2)Σδ_{c_j}γ_j, but the merged display \eqref{NC_delta} states the edge term with coefficient π (a factor 2 discrepancy). The spherical section derives boundary weight π per vertex-edge sum, but \eqref{realembedding} uses pi/2 for the boundary part, so the two final displays disagree with each other and with the sections they merge. Moreover, with the paper's own spherical weights (pi per hemisphere) the Dirac-form scalar product yields a boundary inner-product coefficient pi^2, which contradicts the pi^2/4 stated in the quoted identity \eqref{NC_disc_met}; hence the claimed agreement of \eqref{NC_delta} with NC_disc_met is false as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the constants consistently from the component derivations, fix the conflicting constants in \eqref{NC_delta} and \eqref{realembedding}, and re-verify the claimed agreement with \eqref{NC_disc_met}; this requires deciding which of the conflicting normalizations is correct, which the source does not determine.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central exact Dirac delta representation of the discrete normal cycle, and the real-valued embedding actually fed to the compression algorithm, are mis-normalized and mutually inconsistent; the claim that the resulting scalar product agrees with the published discrete normal-cycle metric fails at least on the boundary term.
issues.title: Merged Dirac delta form and real-valued embedding carry inconsistent constants
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained (fix constants and re-verify an identity) but not routine, since the displayed constants mutually contradict each other and the quoted metric, so a choice of normalization must be made and downstream weights recomputed; the compression method and its guarantees survive with a comparable representation.
